sections.title: String Anagrams (hard)
sections.html:
Given a string and a pattern, find all anagrams of the pattern in the given string.

Anagram is actually a Permutation of a string. For example, “abc” has the following six anagrams:

  1. abc
  2. acb
  3. bac
  4. bca
  5. cab
  6. cba

Write a function to return a list of starting indices of the anagrams of the pattern in the given string.

sections.title: Solution
sections.html: This problem follows the Sliding Window pattern and is very similar to Permutation in a String. In this problem, we need to find every occurrence of any permutation of the pattern in the string. We will use a list to store the starting indices of the anagrams of the pattern in the string.

sections.title: Time Complexity
sections.html: The time complexity of the above algorithm will be O(N+M)O(N + M)O(N+M) where ‘N’ and ‘M’ are the number of characters in the input string and the pattern respectively.

sections.title: Space Complexity
sections.html: The space complexity of the algorithm is O(M)O(M)O(M) since in the worst case, the whole pattern can have distinct characters which will go into the HashMap. In the worst case, we also need O(N)O(N)O(N) space for the result list, this will happen when the pattern has only one character and the string contains only that character.
